stories.headline: Lorry overturns near Soham
stories.brief: A lorry has overturned on a road near Soham. Images from the scene show the vehicle on its side following the incident. Motorists travelling in the area are advised to take care as emergency services deal with the aftermath. No further details regarding the cause of the incident or any potential injuries have been released at this time.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn care homes raise over £500 for Macmillan Cancer Support
stories.brief:
Two care homes in King’s Lynn have raised £514.50 for Macmillan Cancer Support following a joint charity coffee morning. Amberley Hall and Goodwins Hall hosted the event at the Gaywood Church Rooms last Friday, September 25. 

The gathering was attended by residents, members of the public, and the Mayor of West Norfolk, Steve Bearshaw, who was joined by his wife, Marisol. Guests were entertained with live music from singer Emily Blake throughout the morning. Organisers have described the fundraising effort as a success.

stories.headline: Winvic selected for Cambridgeshire road repair trial
stories.brief: Construction firm Winvic has been awarded a contract to lead an innovative road repair trial in Cambridgeshire. The project, reported by Highways News, will see the company test new methods for maintaining the county's highway network. Further details regarding the specific locations or the nature of the repair techniques involved in the trial have not yet been released.

stories.headline: Protest planned in Leverington over asylum seeker hostel proposal
stories.brief:
A peaceful protest is scheduled for this Sunday in Leverington regarding government plans to use Roman Court as a hostel for asylum seekers. Organised by Reform county councillor Chris Tirrell, the gathering will begin at noon at Troughton Way. The proposal aims to house 26 women and children at the site, as part of a wider plan to accommodate 205 asylum seekers across the Fenland district. 

Both the local district council and MP Steve Barclay have expressed opposition to the move. A final decision on the future of the Roman Court site is expected from the government by October 16.

stories.headline: Police appeal for witnesses following King's Lynn collision
stories.brief:
Police are appealing for information following a collision at the Southgates roundabout in King's Lynn last Thursday morning. The incident occurred shortly before 6:30am and involved a white BMW and a motorbike. The motorcyclist was taken to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital with a broken wrist and ankle injuries.

A man in his 40s was arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by dangerous driving and driving while disqualified. He has been released on bail until November 24 while investigations continue. Officers are asking anyone with dashcam footage from the area at the time of the collision to come forward.

stories.headline: Ely man jailed for arson at his own home
stories.brief: A man from Ely has been sentenced to time in prison after starting a fire at his own property. The case, reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, confirms that the individual was convicted of arson. No further details regarding the date of the incident or the length of the custodial sentence have been provided.

stories.headline: Investigation launched following alleged assault at Cambridgeshire school
stories.brief: An investigation is underway following reports of an assault involving a boy at a school in Cambridgeshire. Details regarding the incident remain limited at this stage, but authorities have confirmed that inquiries are currently being carried out. No further information has been released regarding the condition of the student or the specific location of the school involved. We will bring you more updates as they become available.

stories.headline: Record attendance at King’s Lynn and West Norfolk Law Society ball
stories.brief: The King’s Lynn and West Norfolk Law Society held its annual celebration ball at the town’s historic town hall on Friday, September 11. The event, which serves as a key date in the society’s calendar, saw one of its highest attendances in recent years. Legal professionals and members of the local business community gathered for an evening that included a formal dinner, live music from the Soul Sisters, and a speech by Judge Simon Spence. Society president Joshua Shuardson-Hipkin thanked those who attended and the committee for their work in organising the event. The evening was supported by several sponsors, including headline sponsor Cynergy Bank.

stories.headline: Peterborough United managerial appointment delayed
stories.brief: The appointment of Robbie Savage as the new manager of Peterborough United is currently on hold. Reports indicate that the delay is due to an ongoing dispute regarding compensation. No further details have been released regarding when the situation might be resolved or when a final decision is expected.

stories.headline: Campaign launched against East Cambridgeshire wind farm proposals
stories.brief: A new campaign has been established to oppose plans for two wind farms in East Cambridgeshire. The proposed developments are located on Grade 1 agricultural land. No further details regarding the specific locations or the groups involved in the opposition have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Campaign launched against East Cambridgeshire wind farm plans
stories.brief: A new campaign has been established to oppose proposals for two wind farms in East Cambridgeshire. The development plans have drawn criticism due to their proposed location on Grade 1 agricultural land. Further details regarding the specific sites or the groups involved in the opposition have not yet been released.

stories.headline: New craft hub to open on King’s Lynn High Street this weekend
stories.brief:
A new craft hub, Pia’s Place, is set to open on King’s Lynn High Street this weekend. Owned by Gaywood resident Pia Cawston, the shop will offer a variety of creative workshops, including basket weaving, watercolour painting, and children’s activities. The venue also features a selection of vintage items alongside coffee and homemade cake.

The doors open to the public this Saturday from 9am until 3pm, and Sunday from 10am until 4pm. Following the launch, the shop will operate from Wednesday to Sunday, between 9am and 4pm. The owner describes the new venture as a space for all ages to enjoy.

stories.headline: Plans submitted for new East Cambridgeshire wind farm
stories.brief: A new wind farm project has been proposed for East Cambridgeshire. According to reports, the development has the potential to generate enough electricity to power more than 200,000 homes. Further details regarding the specific location and timeline for the construction have not yet been confirmed.

stories.headline: Former Springwood student begins studies at Cambridge
stories.brief:
A former student from Springwood High School in King’s Lynn has begun her university career at Cambridge. Eva Kalabina, who achieved three A* grades and one A in her A-Levels, is now studying Economics, Law, and Environment. 

The 18-year-old credited the support of her teachers at the West Norfolk Academies Trust school for helping her secure her place. Looking ahead, Ms. Kalabina hopes to pursue a career within the technology industry or consultancy. She described her time at the Lynn school as a positive experience that helped her grow both academically and personally.

stories.headline: Emergency lock closures leave boaters stranded in March
stories.brief: Boaters are currently unable to move through March following the introduction of emergency lock closures. The restrictions have left vessels marooned in the area. No further details regarding the cause of the closures or when the locks might reopen have been provided. Those planning to travel through the town by water are advised to be aware of the ongoing disruption.

stories.headline: Top ratings for West Norfolk leisure centres
stories.brief:
Four council-run leisure centres in West Norfolk have been awarded a ‘very good’ rating following a national quality assessment. The sites, managed by Alive West Norfolk, include Lynnsport and St James’ Pool in King’s Lynn, Downham Leisure, and The Oasis in Hunstanton. 

The Quest for Facilities scheme evaluated the centres through mystery visits and independent inspections, focusing on areas such as customer service, safety, and community engagement. In addition to this rating, the service has also received The Active Standard certification from the trade body ukactive. Council officials have praised the staff for their ongoing commitment to maintaining high standards across all four facilities.

stories.headline: Red Arrows to fly over Cambridgeshire this week
stories.brief: Residents across Cambridgeshire are being advised that the Red Arrows are scheduled to fly over the county this week. The display team will be visible from various locations, though specific flight paths and timings have not been confirmed in this report. Those hoping to catch a glimpse of the aircraft are encouraged to keep an eye on the skies throughout the coming days. Further details regarding the exact route and viewing opportunities are expected to be available through local news sources as the week progresses.

stories.headline: Women's football team to face Peterborough United in League Cup
stories.brief: The women's football team is set to host Peterborough United in the opening round of the League Cup. The fixture was confirmed following the latest draw. Fans are now looking ahead to the upcoming match as the side prepares for this first-round encounter.

stories.headline: Long-term lease secured for Ely Museum
stories.brief: Ely Museum has confirmed it will remain at the Old Gaol site for the next century. The institution has successfully secured a new lease agreement that runs until the year 2125. The museum, which is housed in the historic building, will continue to operate from the premises for the foreseeable future.

stories.headline: Courts across West Norfolk deal with a series of recent criminal cases
stories.brief:
Courts in King’s Lynn and Norwich have dealt with a variety of cases over the past week. Three animal rights activists were found guilty of stealing lambs from the King’s Sandringham estate in 2023. Meanwhile, a local man avoided jail after being convicted of stalking and making death threats.

Other hearings included a North Lynn man charged with multiple building site burglaries, and several drink-driving offences across the region. Magistrates also sentenced a man for assaulting emergency workers, while a shoplifter was jailed for repeatedly targeting a King’s Lynn store. Legal proceedings continue for a woman accused of pushing a police officer during an incident in Fakenham.

stories.headline: Vehicle fire reported in Cambridgeshire town centre
stories.brief: Emergency services have responded to a vehicle fire in a Cambridgeshire town centre. Reports indicate that a van caught fire, though no further details regarding the exact location or any potential injuries have been provided at this stage. Local residents are advised to remain aware of potential disruption in the area while the incident is dealt with.

stories.headline: Norwich Road in Wisbech to close for gas pipe replacement
stories.brief:
Drivers in Wisbech are being warned of a lengthy road closure starting next month. Norwich Road will be shut to all vehicles between Churchill Road and Bowthorpe Road from October 5 until December 18. Cadent Gas Ltd is carrying out the work to replace old pipes with new plastic infrastructure. 

While the road will be closed to through traffic, access to local properties will be maintained. A diversion route will be in operation throughout the works. The company says some residents may experience temporary gas supply interruptions and that site teams will provide further information to those affected.

stories.headline: Norfolk County Council outlines budget plans to tackle £36 million shortfall
stories.brief:
Norfolk County Council has unveiled initial budget proposals for the 2027–28 financial year as it works to close a budget gap of nearly £36 million. Cabinet members are set to discuss the draft plans on Monday, October 5, which include over £32 million in identified savings and service efficiencies. 

The proposals feature measures to support adults and families, alongside a review of council tax options. Officials describe the current financial position as challenging due to rising demand for services. If approved, the council will begin a public consultation later this month. A final decision on the budget and council tax rates is expected in February 2027, following further updates on government funding.

stories.headline: Ely GP surgery seeks expansion as patient numbers rise
stories.brief: A GP surgery in Ely is looking to expand its facilities. Reports indicate the practice is currently operating at near capacity. The surgery has submitted plans to increase its space to accommodate the growing demand for local healthcare services.

stories.headline: Police search for Cambridgeshire man
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire police are currently searching for a man wanted in connection with a series of serious domestic assaults. Officers are asking for the public's assistance as they work to locate the individual. Anyone with information regarding his whereabouts is encouraged to contact the authorities.

stories.headline: Debate continues over proposed asylum accommodation in Leverington
stories.brief: A letter published in the Fenland Citizen has criticised local Conservative opposition to plans for a 26-bed asylum seeker hostel at Roman Court in Leverington. The writer argues that the focus on asylum seekers distracts from wider economic issues, such as the cost of living and employment opportunities in the region. The correspondent claims that political resistance to the government-backed accommodation is an attempt to influence voters who might otherwise support other political parties. The letter concludes by stating that refugees are not responsible for the economic challenges currently facing the Fenland area.

stories.headline: West Norfolk venues named in latest Good Beer Guide
stories.brief:
Twenty-eight venues across West Norfolk have been selected for the 2027 edition of the Campaign for Real Ale’s Good Beer Guide. The publication, now in its 54th year, highlights over 4,500 pubs and clubs nationwide that serve high-quality cask ale. 

Among the local entries is King’s Lynn’s Ferry Lane Social Club, which recently hosted a launch event for the guide. The venue, also known as the Ouse Booze, was named the branch’s Club of the Year for 2026. According to CAMRA, all listings are based on independent evaluations by their members. The new guide is available to purchase now for £16.99 through the CAMRA website and selected bookstores.

stories.headline: Nine Cambridgeshire areas identified with concerning crime rises
stories.brief: A report from the Ely Standard has highlighted nine specific areas across Cambridgeshire where recent increases in crime are being described as concerning. The publication identifies these locations as part of a broader look at local safety trends. Residents are encouraged to check the full report for further details on the areas affected.

stories.headline: Half-century milestone for Ely pub regular
stories.brief: A long-standing patron of an Ely pub is celebrating a significant personal milestone. After initially stepping in to help out for just ten minutes, the individual has now spent fifty years working behind the bar. The long-term commitment began with a brief favour and has since turned into a half-century career at the establishment.

stories.headline: Three people injured following incident in Spalding
stories.brief: Three people have sustained injuries following an outbreak of violence in the Lincolnshire market town of Spalding. Details regarding the circumstances of the incident remain limited at this stage. Local authorities are currently managing the situation following the reports of the altercation. We will bring you further updates on this story as more information becomes available.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn Samaritans host bingo night in Walsoken
stories.brief:
The King’s Lynn Samaritans are hosting a bingo event at Walsoken Village Hall on Friday, October 23. Doors are set to open at 6pm, with the first game starting at 7pm. 

The evening will feature prizes, vouchers, a raffle, and refreshments. Attendees can also take part in a cash flyer game, while a free game will be available for children. Rob from Rob’s Bingo will be calling the numbers for the event.

stories.headline: Downham Market dance group performs at King’s Lynn Corn Exchange
stories.brief:
More than 100 young performers from the Downham Market-based group, Legacy Dance, took to the stage this week for their annual showcase. The event, titled SetCase26, was held at the King’s Lynn Corn Exchange on Wednesday, September 16. 

Dancers ranging from four to 25 years old demonstrated skills developed under the guidance of instructor Layla Wilkinson. The performance featured students from all of the group's classes, highlighting the supportive community environment fostered by the organisation. Ms. Wilkinson praised the energy of both the performers and the audience during the successful event.

stories.headline: Ely café supports volunteer in job search
stories.brief: A café in Ely is providing support to a local volunteer as they work to build confidence for future employment. The initiative aims to help the individual, named Rayo, develop the necessary skills and self-assurance required to secure a new job. By volunteering at the café, Rayo is gaining practical experience within the local community.

stories.headline: Former Springwood High student secures place at Imperial College London
stories.brief: A former student from Springwood High School in King’s Lynn has begun his studies at Imperial College London. Kevin Monk is pursuing a career in electrical engineering after achieving four A* grades in his A-Levels. He secured top marks in Maths, Further Maths, Chemistry, and Physics at the school, which is part of the West Norfolk Academies Trust. Mr. Monk credited his teachers for their guidance during his time at the school. Looking ahead, he hopes to eventually work within the semiconductor industry in London.

stories.headline: Peterborough United fans discuss potential new manager
stories.brief: Supporters of Peterborough United are sharing their views regarding reports that Robbie Savage could be considered for the club's managerial position. The speculation follows recent media coverage surrounding the potential appointment. Fans have been reacting to the prospect of the former player taking charge at the club.

stories.headline: Investigation launched following alleged assault at Cambridgeshire school
stories.brief: An investigation is underway following reports of an alleged assault involving a boy at a school in Cambridgeshire. Details regarding the specific location of the school or the circumstances surrounding the incident have not yet been released. Authorities are currently looking into the matter.

stories.headline: Eight-year-old to cycle 70 miles for East Winch Wildlife Centre
stories.brief:
An eight-year-old girl from the region is preparing for a three-day cycling challenge to raise money for the RSPCA East Winch Wildlife Centre. Sophia Sawyer and her father, Ben, will cycle over 70 miles from Lynn to Cromer Pier, starting on Friday, October 2. 

Sophia, who hopes to become a vet, was inspired to fundraise after the family rescued a nest of baby jackdaws last year. She has already exceeded her initial £100 target, with all proceeds going towards food and medicine for injured animals, including seals and hedgehogs. Her mother, Alexandra, and sister, Florence, will provide support throughout the journey. Donations can be made via the family’s JustGiving page.

stories.headline: Plans proposed for large wind turbines on farmland
stories.brief: New proposals have been put forward that could see large-scale wind turbines constructed on agricultural land. According to reports, the project involves the installation of what have been described as gargantuan turbines. Further details regarding the specific locations or the scale of the development have not yet been confirmed. Residents are advised to monitor local planning portals for updates as the situation progresses.

stories.headline: Debris reported on Cambridgeshire road
stories.brief: Motorists in Cambridgeshire are being advised to take care following reports of a large quantity of stones scattered across a local road. The debris has been identified on the carriageway, potentially causing hazards for those travelling through the area. Drivers are encouraged to remain vigilant and adjust their speed accordingly while navigating the affected route. No further details regarding the specific location or the cause of the obstruction have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn Rotary Club marks centenary milestone
stories.brief:
The Rotary Club of King’s Lynn has celebrated one hundred years of community service. Members and guests gathered at the town hall on Friday, September 25, for a black-tie dinner to mark the occasion. Around 120 people attended the event, including representatives from the club’s twin town of Emmerich-am-Rhein in Germany. 

During the evening, club president Michael Douglass highlighted the group’s long-standing support for local, national, and international causes. A new book detailing the club's history, written by member Michael Walker, was also featured. Since the turn of the millennium, the organisation has provided assistance to approximately 150 charities and numerous individuals. The club says it remains committed to supporting the community for the next century.

stories.headline: Peterborough United deny Robbie Savage manager rumours
stories.brief: Peterborough United have dismissed reports suggesting that Robbie Savage has been offered the manager's position at London Road. The club has officially denied that any such offer has been made to the former footballer. The statement follows recent speculation linking him to the vacant role at the club.

stories.headline: Rail replacement buses to run across Cambridgeshire in October
stories.brief: Passengers travelling by train across Cambridgeshire are being warned of disruption throughout the month of October. Major rail improvement works are scheduled to take place across the county during this period. As a result, rail services will be suspended and replaced by bus services for the duration of the upgrades. Travellers are advised to check their journey details before setting off, as these changes will affect routes throughout the region.

stories.headline: Car collides with wall in the Fens
stories.brief: A car has crashed into a wall in the Fens. The incident was reported by the March Chatteris Whittlesey News. No further details regarding the location, time, or any injuries have been provided at this stage.

stories.headline: Campaign launched to improve child road safety in the Fens
stories.brief:
A new road safety initiative called Be Bright Be Seen has been launched across Fenland to help children stay visible as the nights draw in. Sponsored by Ashwood Homes, the campaign is distributing thousands of free reflective keyrings to local schools, sports teams, and youth groups. These can be attached to bags, coats, or bicycles to help pedestrians and cyclists stand out to motorists.

Organisers are also encouraging families to wear bright or reflective clothing during the darker months, particularly after the clocks go back on Sunday, October 25. Teachers and youth leaders can apply for a supply of the free keyrings by visiting the Fenland Citizen website.

stories.headline: North West Norfolk MP calls for stronger chalk stream protections
stories.brief:
North West Norfolk MP James Wild is calling on the government to strengthen planning protections for local chalk streams. Mr Wild has joined a cross-party group of parliamentarians in urging ministers to reconsider current planning policies, which they argue do not sufficiently safeguard these rare habitats. The campaign highlights the importance of sites in Gaywood, Babingley, and Heacham. 

Supporters of the move state that chalk streams are globally scarce and require more robust legal defences against threats such as pollution and over-abstraction. Mr Wild, who is part of an All-Party Parliamentary Group focused on the issue, is advocating for clearer protections to be included in future planning decisions and the forthcoming Clean Water Bill.

stories.headline: New planning applications submitted to Fenland District Council
stories.brief:
Fenland District Council has received a range of new planning applications across the region. In Chatteris, proposals include changing a retail unit at 10 High Street into a hot food takeaway, with a flat planned for the first floor. Other local submissions include plans for new dwellings in Friday Bridge, March, and Wisbech St Mary.

In March, several applications have been lodged regarding the large-scale residential development south of Barkers Lane and east of Wimblington Road, focusing on drainage, lighting, and construction management. Additionally, applications for internal works to a listed building in Chatteris and a commemorative plaque in Wisbech are currently under consideration. Residents can view full details of these applications on the Fenland District Council website.

stories.headline: Former King’s Lynn student secures place at Oxford University
stories.brief:
A former Springwood High School student has begun his studies at the University of Oxford. Merry Enters, 18, is currently reading Philosophy, Politics and Economics at the institution. He achieved A-level results of an A* in Physics, an A in Maths, and a B in Music Technology before securing his place through a late application. 

Mr. Enters credited the support of his teachers at the King’s Lynn school for encouraging his application. While he previously considered a career in music, he is now exploring future roles in economics, consulting, or analysis. He intends to continue playing the guitar as a hobby while he pursues his academic interests.

stories.headline: Lorry overturns on East Cambridgeshire road
stories.brief: A driver has been injured following a road traffic collision in East Cambridgeshire. Emergency services were called to the scene after a lorry overturned on a busy route in the area. Motorists are advised to expect disruption while the incident is dealt with. No further details regarding the condition of the driver or the exact location of the crash have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Investigation launched following death of baby in March
stories.brief: Police have launched an investigation after a baby died in March. A man and a woman from the town have been arrested on suspicion of assault in connection with the incident. Officers remain involved in the case as enquiries continue.

stories.headline: Wisbech Gallery announces winners of OPEN 2026 exhibition
stories.brief:
Wisbech Gallery has revealed the winners of its OPEN 2026 exhibition, which showcases over 90 works from artists across the region. Matt Phelps took the top prize for his entry, while Simon M. Smith was named runner-up. The Young Artist Award, sponsored by EVES, was presented to Calum Seeley.

The exhibition, which launched on September 12, features a variety of disciplines including photography, sculpture, and painting. It remains open to the public free of charge from Wednesday to Saturday, 10am until 4pm, until October 10. Gallery staff have praised the high quality of submissions and the strong turnout during the opening weekend. Further information is available on the gallery’s website.

stories.headline: Fakenham Film Festival receives celebrity support
stories.brief:
The Fakenham Film Festival has received a boost ahead of its opening this Friday, with surprise video messages from Sir Stephen Fry and director John Madden. Organised by the volunteer group Active Fakenham, the three-day event takes place at the Central Cinema from October 2 to October 4.

The festival will showcase around 30 independent films, including dramas, documentaries, and horror features, alongside works by young filmmakers. The programme aims to highlight Norfolk-based stories and independent cinema. The event concludes on Sunday with a red carpet awards finale. Further details and the celebrity messages are available on the Active Fakenham website.

stories.headline: Council to oppose asylum seeker housing plan in Fenland village
stories.brief: Local authorities have announced they will robustly challenge a proposal to accommodate 26 asylum seekers within a Fenland village. The council confirmed its intention to fight the plans, though further details regarding the specific location or the timeline for the development have not been disclosed. Residents are advised to monitor official council updates as the situation progresses.

stories.headline: Police appeal to locate wanted man last seen in Wisbech
stories.brief:
Lincolnshire Police are asking for the public's help to find 34-year-old Davy Hill. He is wanted by officers in connection with an investigation into a rape. Mr Hill was last seen in the Wisbech area, though police believe he may have since travelled elsewhere.

Anyone with information regarding his current whereabouts is urged to contact the police. You can email wanted@lincs.police.uk, quoting reference 26000480721. Alternatively, you can call 101 or report details anonymously through the independent charity Crimestoppers.

stories.headline: Fleetwood Town Under-21s secure win in Peterborough
stories.brief: Fleetwood Town’s Under-21 side has claimed a victory following a match in Peterborough. The result was decided by a goal from Sawkins, who secured the win for the visiting team.

stories.headline: Ten Cambridgeshire pubs recognised for real ale
stories.brief: Ten pubs across Cambridgeshire have been named among the best venues for real ale in the United Kingdom. The recognition comes from the Ely Standard, which highlighted the local establishments for their quality offerings. The list celebrates the top spots for ale enthusiasts within the county.

stories.headline: New Best Start Family Hubs open across Cambridgeshire
stories.brief:
Cambridgeshire County Council has launched five new Best Start Family Hubs, including a site in Wisbech. These centres replace existing child and family facilities, bringing services like health, childcare, housing, and financial advice under one roof. While currently focused on support from pregnancy to age five, the service will eventually expand to assist young people up to age 19, or 25 for those with special educational needs.

The hubs are free to use and open to all families. Launch events are being held at each location throughout this week, offering residents the chance to meet staff and explore the available resources. Further information is also accessible through the council’s network of local sites and online services.

stories.headline: West Norfolk woman completes Ben Nevis climb for hospital unit
stories.brief:
A West Norfolk woman has raised over £540 for the Peddars Way end-of-life unit at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. Jan Mick climbed Ben Nevis in memory of her father, Harry, who passed away earlier this month. 

The challenge took nine hours and 20 minutes to complete, with Jan facing difficult conditions including strong winds, rain, and temperatures dropping to minus four degrees at the summit. Jan, who recently moved to the area from Hertfordshire, chose the climb to honour her father’s active lifestyle. The hospital has expressed its gratitude for the donation, which exceeded the original £200 target. Supporters can still contribute to the fundraiser online.

stories.headline: Government minister apologises for Whittlesey correspondence delay
stories.brief: A government minister has issued an apology after failing to respond to correspondence regarding the discovery of dead fish in Whittlesey. The issue, which was reported by the BBC, centres on a lack of communication from the minister’s office concerning the environmental incident. No further details regarding the cause of the fish deaths or the specific timeline of the correspondence have been provided at this stage.

stories.headline: Fleetwood Town player looks ahead to Peterborough match
stories.brief: Fleetwood Town footballer Costelloe is preparing for the upcoming trip to Peterborough. Following his recent first-team debut, the player has expressed his desire to build on that performance as the squad heads into the fixture.

stories.headline: Plans proposed for two new wind farms in the Fens
stories.brief: Proposals have been submitted for the construction of two new wind farms in the region. The sites earmarked for the potential developments are located near Chatteris and Shippea Hill. No further details regarding the scale or timeline of these projects have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: Norfolk health officials consider future of A&E services
stories.brief:
Health officials in Norfolk are considering plans that could see A&E units at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn and the James Paget Hospital in Gorleston closed. Confidential documents reveal three potential options for future emergency care, with only one retaining full A&E services at all three of the county’s hospitals. Other proposals include downgrading the units to urgent treatment centres or removing major trauma services.

The Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group states that no final decisions have been made and that the documents are part of preliminary work. However, local MPs have expressed strong opposition to any potential downgrades, citing concerns over rural travel times and the impact on patient care.

stories.headline: Wisbech newsagent TG Jones to close in January
stories.brief:
The newsagent and stationer TG Jones has confirmed it will shut its Wisbech branch early next year. The shop, located on the Market Place, is scheduled to close its doors on Saturday, January 9, 2027. The closure is part of a wider, court-approved restructuring plan affecting several of the company's stores across the UK. 

A spokesperson for the retailer expressed regret over the impact on the local community and staff. A closing down sale will be held at the premises before the final closure date. The company stated that its current priority is supporting affected employees while continuing to serve customers during the final weeks of operation.

stories.headline: Three-year driving ban for holidaymaker caught in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
A holidaymaker has been disqualified from driving for three years after being caught over the limit in King’s Lynn. Forty-two-year-old David Canatch, from Gainsborough, was stopped by police on Gayton Road after officers noticed his fog lights were on during clear weather. A breath test revealed he had 45 micrograms of alcohol per 100 millilitres of breath, exceeding the legal limit of 35.

Appearing at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, Mr Canatch pleaded guilty to drink-driving. In addition to the driving ban, he was ordered to pay a £120 fine, a £48 victim surcharge, and £50 in court costs.

stories.headline: Free AI training pilot launched for Cambridge and Peterborough organisations
stories.brief: Organisations across the Cambridge and Peterborough area are being offered the chance to take part in a new artificial intelligence training pilot. The scheme, coordinated by the Cambridge Network, provides training sessions at no cost to participants. The initiative aims to support local groups and businesses looking to develop their understanding of AI technology. Further details regarding the programme and how to register for the pilot are available through the Cambridge Network.

stories.headline: Bus routes cut in Cambridgeshire village despite new shelters
stories.brief: A Cambridgeshire village has seen its bus services withdrawn, despite the recent installation of new bus shelters. The infrastructure project, which cost 16,000 pounds, was completed before the decision to cut the local routes was made. Residents in the area are now facing a loss of public transport links despite the significant investment in the facilities.

stories.headline: Candidates confirmed for Long Sutton by-election
stories.brief: The list of candidates standing in the upcoming by-election for Long Sutton has been officially announced. Residents in the area will head to the polls to select a new representative following the vacancy. Further details regarding the candidates and the polling process are expected to be made available to the public ahead of the vote.

stories.headline: Emergency lock closures leave boaters stranded in March
stories.brief: Boaters are currently unable to move through March following the announcement of emergency lock closures. The restrictions have left vessels marooned in the area. No further details regarding the cause of the closures or a timeline for the reopening of the waterway have been provided at this stage. Those planning to travel through the town by boat are advised to be aware of the disruption.

stories.headline: Opposition grows to Leverington asylum accommodation plans
stories.brief:
Fenland District Council and North East Cambridgeshire MP Steve Barclay have voiced strong opposition to government plans for a 26-bed asylum seeker facility in Leverington. The Home Office proposal for Roman Court is intended to house mothers and babies as part of a wider move toward long-term dispersal accommodation. 

However, local leaders have raised concerns regarding the suitability of the site and the potential for future changes to the facility's use. Mr Barclay has expressed fears that this is the first stage of a broader government policy to bring 205 asylum seekers into the district. No specific timeline for the project has been provided by the Home Office, which says it will continue to engage with local partners.

stories.headline: Improvement work begins at North Lynn ponds
stories.brief:
Maintenance work is starting today at the Loke Road ponds in North Lynn. West Norfolk Council staff are clearing overhanging and diseased trees to improve the habitat for local fish and invertebrates. The project involves cutting back willow trees and removing two ash trees identified as diseased. 

Officials say the work is necessary to prevent rotting leaves from depleting oxygen levels in the water and to reduce excessive shade. The clearance also aims to protect pond liners and dams from damage caused by aggressive willow roots. This initiative is part of a wider pond regeneration programme that began in 2023.

stories.headline: Wisbech fish and chip shop earns national recognition
stories.brief:
A Wisbech takeaway has been named among the best in the country. The Jolly Fryer, located on North End, has secured a place in the top 100 of a new national ranking. The list is compiled by the Fish & Chips app, which evaluates over 3,000 businesses across the UK. 

The rankings are updated monthly and are based on weighted scores from Google and Tripadvisor reviews. According to the app developers, shops cannot pay for inclusion, and the scoring system prioritises establishments with a higher volume of customer feedback.

stories.headline: New quantum eye imaging technology developed for children
stories.brief: Researchers at University College London and the company Siloton have collaborated to adapt quantum-enabled imaging technology specifically for use with children. The project aims to refine eye scanning techniques to better suit younger patients. Further details regarding the implementation or availability of this new diagnostic tool have not yet been released.

stories.headline: Health study results due for Whittlesey pit site
stories.brief: Findings from a health study concerning the controversial pit site in Whittlesey are set to be released. The report, which has been highlighted by the Cambs Times, examines the site that has previously been a subject of local debate. Further details regarding the study's conclusions are expected to be made public soon.

stories.headline: Developer reduces funding pledge for Fenland services
stories.brief: A property developer has withdrawn a fifty-thousand-pound commitment intended to support local services. The pledge was originally made to Fenland District Council. Reports suggest the move has drawn criticism regarding the council's oversight of such agreements. No further details have been provided regarding which specific services will be affected by the loss of this funding or how the council intends to respond to the developer's decision.

stories.headline: Wisbech High Street redevelopment plans approved
stories.brief:
Fenland District Council has approved plans to redevelop a vacant site on Wisbech High Street. The project will see the construction of commercial premises and six one-bedroom flats at numbers 11 and 12, with access provided via Castle Mews. The site has remained empty since the original Grade II listed buildings were demolished in 2020.

During a meeting on Wednesday, September 23, councillors described the two-decade delay in bringing the site back into use as embarrassing. Council leader Chris Boden has called for an explanation regarding previous administrative issues that stalled the development. Local representatives have welcomed the decision, noting that the project is a positive step for the town.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn sleep out raises over £7,000 for local night shelter
stories.brief:
A charity sleep out in King’s Lynn has raised more than £7,000 to support the town’s night shelter. Around 30 people spent Friday night in the grounds of the Minster to experience the challenges of sleeping rough. The funds will help the shelter, which relies entirely on community support and grants, as it prepares to reopen its doors on October 8.

The shelter is now appealing for food donations, including tinned goods, breakfast items, and long-life milk, to stock its cupboards for the winter season. Anyone interested in volunteering or donating can find further information on the King’s Lynn Night Shelter website or by calling 01553 776109.

stories.headline: Peterborough walkway project costs rise following skeleton discovery
stories.brief: The budget for a new walkway in Peterborough has increased by 1.6 million pounds. This additional expenditure follows the discovery of a skeleton at the construction site. The project, which aims to improve pedestrian access in the area, now faces higher costs due to the archaeological find. Further details regarding the impact on the construction timeline have not been released.

stories.headline: Conservative Party begins candidate selection for two Cambridgeshire seats
stories.brief: The Conservative Party has officially opened the process to select candidates for two parliamentary seats in Cambridgeshire. According to reports from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, the party is now accepting applications for these constituencies. Further details regarding the specific locations or the timeline for these selections have not yet been released. Residents interested in local political developments are advised to monitor official party announcements for updates as the selection process moves forward.

stories.headline: Financial loss expected for March bank site project
stories.brief: Fenland District Council is facing a projected loss of eight hundred thousand pounds regarding the regeneration of a bank site in March. Reports indicate the local authority expects the shortfall as work progresses on the development. No further details regarding the specific site or the reasons for the deficit have been provided at this stage.

stories.headline: Wisbech academy hosts talks on the future of Fenland soil
stories.brief:
The Green Skills Academy in Wisbech has hosted a collaborative session focused on the future of agriculture and peat soil in the Fens. The event brought together the Fenland Environmental Network and the non-profit group Fenland SOIL to discuss the long-term sustainability of the local landscape. 

Organisers say the meeting provided a space for education providers and environmental groups to share expertise on land use and food production. The session aligns with the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Local Skills Improvement Plan, which highlights sustainable land management as a priority for the region. The College of West Anglia says the initiative aims to help students gain the skills needed to support the local economy’s shift toward a more sustainable future.

stories.headline: MP calls for Ely Junction upgrades to improve Fen Line services
stories.brief:
South West Norfolk MP Terry Jermy is urging the Transport Secretary to prioritise upgrades to Ely Junction. Following a summer that saw hundreds of cancellations on the Fen Line, Mr Jermy met with the Fen Line Users’ Association to discuss the impact on passengers in King’s Lynn, Downham Market, and Watlington. 

The MP highlighted issues including poor service reliability, cleanliness, and faulty air conditioning. While acknowledging that extreme weather has affected local peat soils, he argued that many delays remain avoidable. Mr Jermy is now pushing for the project to be included in the next government Spending Review to boost regional growth. Meanwhile, a new scheme launched on September 20 now allows passengers to use alternative operators if their train is cancelled.

stories.headline: Government consultation begins on Cambridgeshire local government changes
stories.brief:
A government consultation regarding the reorganisation of local government in Cambridgeshire is now underway. Residents are being invited to learn more about the proposed changes, specifically focusing on the details of option B. 

The consultation process is being highlighted by Cambridge City Council. Those living across the region can participate to understand how these potential structural adjustments might affect local administration. Further information on the specific proposals is available through official government channels.

stories.headline: Prison sentence for Cambridgeshire Crème Egg thief
stories.brief: A person has been jailed for stealing Crème Eggs. According to Cambridgeshire Constabulary, the individual was convicted following the theft of the confectionery items. No further details regarding the location or the specific circumstances of the incident have been released by the police at this time.

stories.headline: Peterborough Sports look to bounce back
stories.brief: Peterborough Sports are preparing for their next fixture following a recent defeat. The team is looking to recover quickly from the result, with players and staff focusing on an immediate opportunity to improve their performance. Supporters will be watching to see how the side responds in their upcoming match.

stories.headline: Proposals submitted for over 1,600 new homes in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: New plans have been unveiled that could see the construction of more than 1,600 homes in Cambridgeshire. According to reports from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, the proposed development has the potential to extend the footprint of the city. No further details regarding the specific location or timeline for the project have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: Historic Penny Farthing remains on display in March
stories.brief: A Penny Farthing bicycle has been a landmark feature above a garage in March for 115 years. The vintage cycle continues to be displayed at the site, marking over a century of local history.

stories.headline: World Grand Prix success for Luke Woodhouse
stories.brief: Darts player Luke Woodhouse has secured victory at the World Grand Prix. The professional darts player, who has connections to the local area, claimed the title following a successful performance in the tournament. The result was reported by Darts World Magazine.

stories.headline: Changes to waste collection in East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Residents in East Cambridgeshire are seeing a change to how their household waste is collected. The local authority is moving away from the use of bags for rubbish, replacing them with wheelie bins. This update marks a new era for waste management services across the district. Householders are advised to look out for their new bins as the transition takes place.

stories.headline: New crematorium and bereavement centre opens in East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Residents in East Cambridgeshire can now view the interior of the district’s newly completed crematorium and bereavement centre. The facility, which has recently been unveiled, is designed to provide local funeral services and support for the community. Further details regarding the site’s operations and services are expected to be available to the public as the centre begins its work.

stories.headline: Robbie Savage declines to comment on Peterborough United rumours
stories.brief: Former footballer Robbie Savage has refused to address ongoing speculation linking him to a managerial role at Peterborough United. Reports circulating in the sports media have suggested a potential connection between the broadcaster and the club, but Savage has remained tight-lipped regarding the claims. No official statement has been issued by Peterborough United concerning the vacancy or any prospective candidates.

stories.headline: Care Network Cambridgeshire marks 40th anniversary
stories.brief: Care Network Cambridgeshire is celebrating four decades of service to the local community. The organisation reached the milestone following a busy year, having provided support to 2,479 people throughout 2025.

stories.headline: Robbie Savage linked to Peterborough United role
stories.brief: Reports from The League Paper suggest that Robbie Savage could be set for a move into the English Football League with Peterborough United. The former professional footballer has been connected to a position at the club, though no further details regarding the nature of the potential role have been confirmed. Fans of the Posh will be watching closely to see if these links develop into a formal appointment in the coming weeks.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire crematorium evacuated shortly after opening
stories.brief: A newly opened crematorium in Cambridgeshire has been evacuated. The facility, which only began serving the public a few weeks ago, was cleared following an incident. No further details regarding the cause of the evacuation or the current status of the site have been provided.

stories.headline: Peterborough United dismiss managerial speculation
stories.brief: Peterborough United have officially denied reports regarding the club’s managerial position that circulated this past Sunday. Despite the club's statement, a prominent supporter has publicly suggested that Robbie Savage remains a genuine contender for the role. No further details regarding the club's leadership plans have been confirmed at this time.

stories.headline: Nine road closures announced across Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Motorists travelling across Cambridgeshire are being advised of nine upcoming road closures in the region. The Hunts Post reports that these disruptions are currently in place, and drivers are encouraged to check their routes before setting off. While specific locations and durations for the closures have not been detailed, residents are urged to stay informed about potential travel delays. Please plan your journeys accordingly to avoid any inconvenience while these works are carried out.

stories.headline: Peterborough Sports look to bounce back
stories.brief: Peterborough Sports are preparing for their next fixture following a recent defeat. The team is looking to recover quickly from the result, with players and staff focused on an immediate opportunity to improve their performance.

stories.headline: Smoke prompts evacuation at new crematorium during testing
stories.brief: A newly built crematorium has been evacuated following reports of increased smoke levels. The incident occurred while the facility was undergoing routine testing. No further details regarding the cause of the smoke or potential damage have been released at this time.

stories.headline: MP Stephen Barclay raises further questions regarding Saxon Pit
stories.brief: North East Cambridgeshire MP Stephen Barclay has submitted new questions concerning the Saxon Pit site in Whittlesey. The details of the inquiry follow recent reports regarding the location. No further information has been provided at this stage regarding the specific nature of the questions or the expected response from relevant authorities.

stories.headline: Evacuation at new crematorium following smoke during testing
stories.brief: A newly built crematorium has been evacuated after reports of increased smoke levels. The incident occurred while the facility was undergoing testing. No further details regarding the cause of the smoke or the current status of the site have been released.

stories.headline: Sutton extend lead in local derby
stories.brief: Sutton have moved 35 points clear at the top of the table following a decisive win in their latest derby match. The result, reported by the Spalding South Holland News, sees the side strengthen their position in the league standings.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire man convicted of attempted murder
stories.brief: A Cambridgeshire man has been convicted of attempting to kill his partner. The court heard that the defendant carried out a violent attack, which involved both stabbing the victim and attempting to electrocute her. The case was reported by the Hunts Post.
